entity.name: Tayyab Ahmed
entity.description: I am an independent software engineer and open-source maintainer based in India, building low-latency media systems and developer tools. I am the primary maintainer of Sync.audio, an open-source zero-hardware silent audio broadcasting protocol for Smart TV and web runtimes. My goal is to establish sub-50ms Web Audio and WebSocket streaming standards that allow multi-user personal listening without dedicated hardware splitters or dongles.

projects.name: Sync.audio
projects.description: Sync.audio is an MIT-licensed, local-first low-latency silent audio broadcasting engine for Smart TVs (Fire OS / Vega OS) and web browsers. It captures audio from host media streams via AudioWorklet background threads and relays binary PCM chunks over WebSockets to client mobile devices. Clients process audio in custom Web Audio player worklets, offering real-time lip-sync calibration, sub-50ms latency telemetry, and zero-hardware setup without native app installs. This grant will fund core DSP engine optimization, low-level TV platform web shell integration, dynamic lip-sync drift calibration, and public maintainer documentation.
